==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|visiten}}, from {{der|en|fro|visiter}}, from {{der|en|la|vīsitō}}, frequentative of {{m|la|vīsō||behold, survey}}, from {{m|la|videō||see}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=1871746711}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|osx|wīsōn|t=to visit, afflict}}, archaic {{cog|de|weisen|t=to visit, afflict}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|sēċan||to visit}} and {{m|ang|sōcn||a visit}}.

The noun is from {{bor|en|fr|visite}} or the verb.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=7308969320}}</ref> {{doublet|en|visite}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvɪzɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-visit.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪzɪt|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|vis|it}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To habitually [[go]] to (someone in distress, sickness etc.) to [[comfort]] them. (Now generally merged into later senses, below.) {{defdate|from 13th c.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To go and [[meet]] (a person) as an act of [[friendliness]] or [[sociability]]. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|She decided to '''visit''' her grandparents for Christmas.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} Of God: to [[appear]] to (someone) to [[comfort]], [[bless]], or [[chastise]] or [[punish]] them. (Now generally merged into later senses, below.) {{defdate|from 13th c.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|1|68|passage=[God] hath '''visited''' and redeemed his people.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Ruth|1|6|passage=Then she arose with her daughters in law, that she might return from the country of Moab: for she had heard in the country of Moab how that the {{smallcaps|Lord}} had '''visited''' his people in giving them bread.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|now|rare}} To [[punish]], to inflict [[harm]] {{m|en|upon}} (someone or something). {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Gibbon Roman Empire|volume=68
|passage=Her life was spared by the clemency of the emperor, but he '''visited''' the pomp and treasures of her palace.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} Of a sickness, misfortune etc.: to [[afflict]] (someone). {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1890|author=w:James George Frazer|title=w:The Golden Bough
|passage=There used to be a sharp contest as to where the effigy was to be made, for the people thought that the house from which it was carried forth would not be '''visited''' with death that year.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To inflict [[punishment]], [[vengeance]] for (an offense) {{m|en|on}} or {{m|en|upon}} someone. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#* {{quote-video game|en|developer=Bungie|authorlink=Bungie|title=w:Halo 3|publisher=w:Microsoft Game Studios|date=25 September 2007|system=w:Xbox 360|level=[https://www.halopedia.org/Terminal_(Halo_3)#The_terminals Terminal Six (Legendary)]|passage=05-032 was right about one thing: there is only one way to defeat the enemy, and that is to '''visit''' utter annihilation on it.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=John Mullan|journal=The Guardian|date=2 Dec 2011
|passage=If this were an Ibsen play, we would be thinking of the sins of one generation being '''visited''' upon another, he said.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To go to (a shrine, temple etc.) for [[worship]]. (Now generally merged into later senses, below.) {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[go]] to (a place) for pleasure, on an errand, etc. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=19|passage=Nothing was too small to receive attention, if a supervising eye could suggest improvements likely to conduce to the common welfare. Mr. Gordon Burnage, for instance, personally '''visited''' dust-bins and back premises, accompanied by a sort of village bailiff, going his round like a commanding officer doing billets.}}
#* {{quote-web|en|year=2018|url=https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/china-s-melting-glacier-brings-visitors-concern-over-climate-change/4627742.html|title=VOA Learning English > China's Melting Glacier Brings Visitors, Adds to Climate Concerns
|site=learningenglish.voanews.com
|passage=Each year, millions of people '''visit''' the 4,570-meter-high Baishui Glacier in southern China.  [[File:Each year, millions of people visit.ogg]]}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A single act of [[visit#Verb|visiting]].
#: {{ux|en|Next time you're in Manchester, give me a '''visit'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|We paid a quick '''visit''' to James on the way up to Scotland.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1899|author=w:Stephen Crane
|title=s:Twelve O'Clock|chapter=1
|passage=There was some laughter, and Roddle was left free to expand his ideas on the periodic '''visits''' of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up […].”}}
# {{lb|en|medicine|insurance}} A [[meeting]] with a [[doctor]] at their [[surgery]] or the doctor's at one's [[home]].
